messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cholesky_factor_corr
parts:
Do you want the correlations to be positive or the
cholesky factor to be only positive? The latter can
be done with transforms and a Jacobian following the
way we do the Cholesky factor itself. The former would
be easy for a 2 x 2 correlation matrix, but I don't know
how to do it for anything larger.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cholesky_factor_corr
parts:
On Saturday, January 28, 2017 at 7:55:19 AM UTC-5, Vishv Jeet wrote:
Thank you. I want the correlations to be all positive, I did'nt realize that keeping cholesky factor positive is an overkill. I will work out the Jacobian.

Yes, this is the difficulty. There are correlation matrices with all positive correlations for which the lower-triangular elements of the Cholesky factor have mixed signs. And Cholesky factors with all positive lower-triangular elements when multiplied together only cover a subset of the correlation matrices with all positive correlations.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cholesky_factor_corr
parts:
A Gaussian with positive correlations is exchangeable, and
as the dimensions increase it will asymptote to a hierarchical
model.  So you probably just want to just build a hierarchical 
model explicitly.
